title: Schema Evolution Coordinator + Telemetry Hydrator for usage event ingestion
creator: Ava Moreno
description:
Problem: Usage events arriving at the console ingestion tier come from multiple SDK/agent versions and external integrations; over time fields are renamed, nested shapes change, and optional fields appear/disappear. Current validation rejects many historical variants or defers expensive conversions to downstream consumers leading to missed metrics and noisy DLQ churn.

Goal: Implement a Schema Evolution Coordinator (SEC) and a lightweight Telemetry Hydrator that sit in the ingestion pipeline to: (1) track known schema versions and transforms, (2) apply deterministic, testable upgrades/downgrades to a canonical internal shape, (3) enrich events with derived fields used by dashboards (route resolution, model_family, inferred_tier), and (4) surface structured validation failures with actionable error codes.

Scope: 
- SEC is a small service that holds transform rules (protobuf->protobuf transforms + WASM hooks for edge cases) and performs version negotiation.
- Hydrator is a stateless, high-throughput process (Rust worker) that applies cheap enrichments and canonicalization before writing to Kafka topic console.events.canonical.
- Validation step remains but is split into fast-path (schema + type checks) and slow-path (semantic checks with calling policies). Slow-path failures go to DLQ with trace id and transform metadata.

Acceptance criteria: 
- <1% additional p50 latency in the ingest fast-path at 99th percentile throughput.
- >99.9% of events accepted into canonical topic after transformation for last 12 months of known variants.
- Structured failure schema implemented (error_code, version, transform_id, sample_payload_reference) and DLQ consumers documented.
- E2E smoke tests and a conformance test suite (fixtures for historical SDKs) in CI.

Design decisions and rationale: 
- Canonical shape defined as protobuf to enable compact schemas and deterministic upgrades. Protobuf chosen because many existing telemetry types already use typed messages elsewhere in infra.
- Transform rules versioned in git; runtime loads stable snapshots and supports hot-reload for emergency fixes.
- Use WASM for a small set of exceptional transformations to avoid frequent service deploys for edge rewrites. Keep majority of transforms as declarative field mappings to optimize JIT compilation in the worker.
- Hydrator keeps transformations idempotent and attaches a transform provenance header (transform_id, applied_at) for auditability.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Misapplied transform breaks metrics. Mitigate by canarying transforms on a sample stream and gate via console rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
- Risk: Increased latency. Mitigate with SIMD-friendly Rust implementation, parallel workers, and a fast-path that skips hydrating when input already declares canonical_version.

Testing plan: 
- Conformance tests (fixtures from 2019-2026 SDKs) in CI.
- Load test against staging with production-like token mix using k6 and internal telemetry replayer.
- Canary rollout with real traffic and metric comparison (event counts, model_id cardinality, route coverage).

Rollout plan: 
1) Deploy SEC in read-only mode with transforms loaded but not applied; Hydrator dry-run mode logs diffs.
2) Enable 1% traffic rewrite and run for 48 hours. Validate dashboards.
3) Ramp to 25% then 100% with health gates.

Documentation and artifacts: 
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONSOLE/pages/Schema+Evolution+Coordinator+Design (design draft)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-backend/pull/1287 (SEC prototype)
- Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/ingest-schema-health (ingest healthboard)
